n: Moses addresses a hard case: someone claiming spiritual gifts — a prophet or a person who receives dreams — who backs up their message with a miraculous sign.

f.w: a dreamer of dreams
a sign or a wonder

n: Even if the sign actually happens, the message itself is the test. Anyone urging Israel to follow other gods is false, no matter what wonders they perform.

f.w: the sign or the wonder come to pass

n: Signs alone do not prove truth. God allows such tests to reveal whether his people truly love him with their whole heart.

f.w: the LORD your God proveth you

n: Six strong verbs describe true discipleship: walk after him, revere him, keep his commandments, obey his voice, serve him, and cling to him.

f.w: cleave unto him

n: Under the law of Moses, leading Israel into idolatry was treated as treason against the God who had freed them, and it carried the death penalty.

f.w: redeemed you out of the house of bondage
f.g: Redeem = to buy back or free a slave.

f.w: put the evil away from the midst of thee

n: The test gets personal: what if a sibling, child, spouse, or closest friend quietly tries to lead you toward other gods? Loyalty to God must come first.

f.w: the wife of thy bosom
which is as thine own soul
f.g: As dear to you as yourself.

f.w: entice thee secretly

n: It doesn’t matter whether those gods belong to neighbors close by or to distant lands — none of them are to be followed.

f.w: from the one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth

n: No hiding it, no covering for them out of affection. Family ties could not shield someone trying to destroy the covenant community.

f.w: neither shall thine eye pity him
conceal

n: The witness who was enticed was to lead the execution, then the community joined in. This placed the gravest responsibility on the accuser.

f.w: thine hand shall be first upon him

n: Stoning was a public, communal punishment. Many later rabbis and modern readers note these laws were for ancient Israel’s theocratic setting; Jesus taught a higher law of mercy.

f.w: thou shalt stone him with stones

n: The punishment served as a deterrent: all Israel would hear and be warned away from such wickedness.

f.w: all Israel shall hear, and fear

n: A third case: rumors that an entire Israelite town has turned to idolatry.

f.w: If thou shalt hear say

n: Troublemakers have led the whole town astray to worship unknown gods.

f.w: the children of Belial
f.g: Belial = worthlessness; “sons of Belial” means wicked, good-for-nothing men.

n: Before any action, the report must be carefully investigated. Justice requires certainty, not gossip.

f.w: inquire, and make search, and ask diligently

n: If it proves true, the town was to be treated like a Canaanite city under the ban — utterly destroyed.

f.w: destroying it utterly
f.g: Hebrew ḥerem — devoting something entirely to God by destruction.

n: Nothing could be kept as plunder. The whole city was burned as an offering to God and left as a permanent ruin.

f.w: an heap for ever
f.g: Hebrew tel — a mound of ruins.

f.w: every whit

n: Keeping even a little of the devoted things would bring the curse on Israel — as Achan later learned. Purging evil makes room for God’s mercy and growth.

f.w: the cursed thing

n: God’s compassion and blessing follow obedience — listening to his voice and doing what is right in his sight.

f.w: hearken to the voice of the LORD
